_comment: The code that produced the committed rows, captured as git BLOB hashes of the
WORKING TREE -- what the sweep actually executes, not what is committed.
Written by examples/research/write_provenance.py as part of the MEASUREMENT
path -- never derived from HEAD at render time, which would name whatever is
checked out now rather than what measured the rows, and would silently
reattribute every row after the next harness commit. Not stale: false.
`tree_digests` covers every .py under the tracked trees, because naming two
files is not the measurement's code identity: the harness executes blockers,
indexes, embedders and metrics that can change what a row means.
`verified_unchanged_during_run` is the check that none of it moved mid-sweep;
without it no single hash describes all the rows.
`driver_digest` covers the *.sh sweep drivers separately, because they decide
which cells RAN rather than what a number means. A driver edit is recorded in
`drivers_unchanged_during_run` and is NOT fatal -- drivers get repaired
mid-sweep -- but it is never silent: the *.py-only digest used to certify such
an edit as 'unchanged'.
CAPTURED RETROACTIVELY: this sweep finished before write_provenance.py
existed, so its --start/--finish hooks did not run. Values are derived from
git at the measuring commit (see head_when_sweep_started), and the
unchanged-during-run check was performed after the fact with
`git log --since=<started> --until=<finished> -- <tracked trees>`, which is
empty. Future runs capture this automatically via run_lfm25.sh.
The tree digests are therefore COMMIT-derived, not working-tree-derived:
they reproduce from a clean checkout of head_when_sweep_started, but they
cannot see uncommitted edits that may have been present while the sweep
ran. `dirty_at_start` is null for that reason -- unobservable after the
fact, and recording [] would assert a clean tree that nobody checked.
The sweep DRIVERS were edited while this run was in flight (see
drivers_changed_during_run): the memory guard was rewritten after an OS
kill, a resume script was added, and the study selector landed. Those
changed which cells ran and when -- not what any number means, which is
why the *.py digests above are still stable and these are reported apart.
drivers_changed_during_run: 2a6ecb3 feat(lfm25): LFM25_STUDY selector so a partial run can finish the rest [examples/research/run_lfm25.sh]
6012078 chore(lfm25): resume script for the cell lost to the OS kill [examples/research/resume_lfm25_study_a.sh]
1491883 fix(ladder): guard on available memory, not on the swap derivative [examples/research/run_ladder.sh]
